http_semantics.note: On wait=false the client-side error (empty/wrong-dimension vector) is returned as HTTP 200 pure success acknowledgement with NO business error code at all (script reads status field: 'acknowledged'); the identical payload with wait=true yields HTTP 400 'Vector dimension error: expected dim: 4, got 0/3/5' (script header comment quoting server message). Categorized under 2xx because the client error is swallowed inside a success envelope; the failure surfaces nowhere (no error code, no log feedback channel — see source_grounding).

contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: Candidate dispatch carries NO constraint_id (vein-derived). Nearest semantic anchors supplied by builder from structured_contract.json: (1) behavioral qdrant_behavioral_points_upsert_001: 'with wait=false client receives acknowledge-only response immediately; eventual consistency before searchable' / category 'response status acknowledged; data may not be retrievable yet' (JSON lines 4597-4608). (2) doc behavior line (raw_knowledge.md:168, contract source https://api.qdrant.tech/v-1-18-x/api-reference/points/upsert-points): 'behavioral: 200 ok; 400 invalid payload/vector dim mismatch; 404 collection missing; with wait=false client gets acknowledge-only response immediately'. (3) secondary: qdrant_state_points_batch_001 'batch operations execute sequentially in submitted order' (JSON 4359-4368); qdrant_state_vectors_update_001 'update_vectors: unspecified named vectors remain unchanged' (JSON 4392-4401).
contract_grounding.note: The documented behavior line claims '400 invalid payload/vector dim mismatch' with no wait-qualification; observation shows the same payload returning 200 on wait=false and being permanently dropped (not deferred: valid async control id=99 landed, readback after 2s, point-1 vector unchanged). 'Acknowledged' eventual-consistency semantics ('data may not be retrievable YET') do not cover 'never retrievable and client can never learn why'. Hence violates=true against the doc behavior line; the early-ack itself is by-design (see source_grounding), the defect claim is the validation-result feedback channel being absent.

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: actix update_api.rs upsert_points/update_vectors/update_batch (wait flag from query) → src/common/update.rs update() :1228 WaitUntil::from(wait=false)=WaitUntil::Wal → toc point_ops.rs update() :554 → collection point_ops.rs update_from_client() :144 → replica_set/update.rs update_with_consistency :145 → update_local :41 → local_shard shard_ops.rs submit_update :60 [NO vector validation on this path; needs_callback()=false → sender=None; WAL write + enqueue] → await_update_result :184 (None,_) → UpdateStatus::Acknowledged → HTTP 200. CONCURRENTLY: update_worker.rs consumes UpdateSignal::Operation → update_worker_internal → shard segments → segment/entry.rs upsert_point :661 check_named_vectors → common/mod.rs check_vector_against_config :196-200 WrongVectorDimension → worker :151 Err(update_err) → send_feedback(sender=None) :32 if-let misses → error dropped with no log. Net effect: validation exists and DOES run, but only after the HTTP 200 has been sent, and its failure has no delivery channel on the wait=false path — matching the observed 400(sync)/200-then-dropped(async) split exactly. update_vectors (entry.rs :683 same check) and batch (same UpdateSignal pipeline) share the identical structure.
source_grounding.verification_outcome_note: The early-acknowledgement itself is explicit by-design (WaitUntil::Wal doc comment: 'Corresponds with wait=false, acknowledging immediately'). The validation is NOT absent — it exists at the segment write layer and runs in the background worker. What is NOT covered by any design comment: send_feedback silently discards the validation error when sender=None (no log, no feedback channel), so the doc behavior line '400 invalid payload/vector dim mismatch' (unqualified by wait) is only honored on the wait=true path. This is the documented-vs-implemented gap the candidate observed; classification by_design_in_source reflects the intentional async architecture, with the silent-drop detail recorded for the auditor.

mundane_explanation.surviving: by_design_wal_acknowledged (PARTIAL): source comments explicitly design wait=false as early WAL-ack (WaitUntil::Wal). The design intent covers the early 200, but NOT the observed consequence documented here: the background validation failure is discarded with no error surface at all (send_feedback sender=None drops it without logging), while the API doc behavior line promises 400 for invalid vector dim without wait-qualification. The doc-vs-implementation inconsistency survives the by-design defense.
